note: Intentional behavior changes, each citing the change-log entry that documents it. Patterns: file (regex over the normalized relative path), path (regex over the index-free JSON path, e.g. tasks[].status; absent = whole-file or text differences), kind (added | removed | changed | only-recorded | only-replayed | equality-structure), recorded / replayed (regex over the value preview), task (regex over the task id), fixtures / variants (scope, on a pattern or on the whole entry), withinCostRounding. An entry with divergence: true may also cover exact-match content; it must be scoped to fixtures and variants at entry level, and the acceptance test asserts its cause separately. legacyIdentical: true matches only a recorded-only file whose replayed copy was found byte-identical at the legacy .pi/workflows location.

entries.citation: docs/core-port.md WP4c-1 "Executor selection" and change log 11
entries.reason: The run record freezes the selected executor ({id, source, descriptor}) as run.executor; pi-workflow had one implicit executor. The replay registers its descriptor as executor "pi" (default tier).

entries.citation: docs/core-port.md WP4c-1 "R#9, R#10, R#12, R#5" (R#10) and change log 8
entries.reason: The terminal mapping records the session the executor kept (ownedSession on the terminal event) as tasks[].ownedSessions so retention can delete exactly those sessions. The Pi adapter reports a kept session for every requested session id; pi-workflow kept Pi sessions without recording them. Since WP12a (docs/core-port.md WP12a change log 1) the engine requests a kept session only with experimental same-session repair, so default replays show no such difference.

entries.citation: docs/core-port.md WP4b change log 4 and "What launch provenance digests now"; WP4c-1 "Pi executor (WP6)" table (extension isolation, generated extension wrappers)
entries.reason: workflow_artifact is served by the artifact MCP server configured by <task>/artifact-access.json instead of a generated Pi extension wrapper (workflow-artifact-extension.ts). Launch provenance digests the access config and the MCP server spec (artifacts.configSha256/serverSpecSha256, artifactBinding.configPathSha256/configBytesSha256/serverSpecSha256) instead of the wrapper path and bytes, and records no Pi extension list or noExtensions flag.

entries.citation: docs/runtime-port.md "Attempt artifacts" (stderr.log: runtime diagnostics, empty on a clean completion)
entries.reason: The task stderr.log is the runtime attempt stderr.log, which holds runtime diagnostics only. The recorded file was the Pi CLI's own stderr (its session notice). Adapters keep raw CLI output in their own attempt artifacts.

An executor attempt has no process exit code (the executor contract reports a terminal event), so the runtime result.json records exitCode null; the raw-artifact integrity stamp copies the runtime terminal record. The task's own exitCode is still derived from the status (0 for completed).

Run usage rollups sum only what model tasks observed: support tasks (no model call) no longer contribute zeros, so a token class no task reported is absent (unknown) instead of 0. Recorded pi-workflow rollups carried 0 or a provider total for reasoning/cache-creation/total tokens.

Executor usage arrives as SDK UsageEvents (input, output, cached, cost, source), summed by the runtime into result.json metadata.usage. Reasoning, cache-write and total token counts and the provider/model of the attempt are not part of the executor event contract v0, so task and run usage records no longer carry reasoningTokens, totalTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens, provider or model, and usage.attempts[].raw is the runtime summary instead of Pi's usage object. Input, output, cache-read tokens and cost still match (exact-match rule run-usage-totals). The run rollup then reports reasoning/total/cache-write tokens as absent, or as 0 when a support task contributes its zero usage. The same applies to the usage a foreach batch leader records for its physical execution (foreachBatches[].physicalExecution.usage).

The runtime rounds summed usage cost to 12 decimals (src/runtime/orchestrate/execute.ts summarizeUsage), so a recorded 0.013680000000000001 becomes 0.01368. Only values equal after that rounding are covered.

entries.citation: docs/core-port.md WP1b change log 6 (WP4b change log 1: run state .pi/workflows → .agent-workflow/workflows)
entries.reason: The original bundled report helpers (deep-review, impact-review, spec-review, deep-research) write their sidecars with join(cwd, ".pi", "workflows", runId, "tasks", taskId, …). Under agent-workflow they land at the legacy path outside the run directory; the comparison found each one there, byte-identical to the recording (legacyIdentical). The sidecars are not ledger input (the helpers say so) and no task output depends on them.

entries.citation: docs/core-port.md WP1b change log 6 (WP4b change log 1: run state .pi/workflows → .agent-workflow/workflows, no fallback)
entries.reason: The original spec-review helper spec-requirement-source.mjs reads upstream source-manifest.json / control.json from the hard-coded `.pi/workflows/<run>/tasks/<task>/`, which agent-workflow no longer writes. Its evidence gate then reports missing_requirement_source_proof / absent_or_invalid_requirement_scope, so the task-6 partition control differs; task 7 (verify) gets a prompt with that different control digest, which no recording has, so the replay executor refuses it before consume (replay miss) and task 7 fails; task 8 (render) renders the degraded partition. Exactly these three tasks and the run aggregates over them diverge (since docs/core-port.md WP12a change log 3 the aggregates include usage.totalTokens and usage.cacheCreationInputTokens, which the runtime now sums). The acceptance test asserts the cause (the task-6 issues and the task-7 miss at the task-6 digest line) and that the state-path-migrated variant, which migrates only that literal, has no unexplained difference.

entries.citation: docs/runtime-port.md change log 1 (Backends: a resolved backend is the executor id)
entries.reason: The foreach batch receipt records the runtime result's backend. pi-subagent resolved the backend to "headless"; in the runtime a resolved backend is the executor id (the replay executor stands in for "pi").

entries.citation: docs/core-port.md WP1b change log 7 (C2/WP10: workflow_web_* tools and the web-source cache removed)
entries.reason: The recorded deep-research run had the workflow_web_* tools: the engine generated a Pi extension wrapper per web-using task (workflow-web-source-extension.ts) and the tools filled the run's web-source-cache/. Both are gone with C2; the replay neither generates the wrapper nor recreates the cache (the recorded workers' final texts, which quote the fetched sources, are replayed verbatim).

entries.citation: docs/core-port.md WP1b change log 7 (C2/WP10) and change log 5 (executor refusal before READY fails the launch at once)
entries.reason: Expected result, not a comparison: the original deep-research spec asks for the removed workflow_web_* tools, so the Pi executor refuses tasks 11, 12, 13 (research-questions items), 4 (normalize-claims) and 9 (final-audit) before any effect (CAPABILITY_MISSING), the dependent foreach stage materializes no items and the final render blocks. Every difference after the plan stage follows from that refusal. The acceptance test asserts the refusal exactly (tasks, code, message, statuses, the single served launch) instead; the engine-only variant compares the rest of the run.

The task backend adds the workflow_artifact tool guidelines (WORKFLOW_ARTIFACT_TOOL_GUIDELINES, the MCP server instructions) to the system prompt of every task that has the artifact server, because not every MCP client shows server instructions to the model (Pi 1.1 does not). pi-workflow's Pi extension registered them as tool guidelines instead.

differences.replayed: ^# Workflow Artifact Tool\n- Use workflow_artifact to inspect upstream workflow artifacts

entries.reason: The system-prompt hint for the workflow_web_* source-card tools is gone with those tools (C2). The original deep-research spec still lists them, so its recorded system prompts carry the hint and the replayed ones do not.

differences.recorded: ^Workflow web-source tools return compact source cards\.

entries.reason: WP4d records the pre-launch executor probe and per-stage B4 negotiation (effective capabilities, reports, degradations, preview) on the run as run.capabilityNegotiation; pi-workflow had no capability negotiation. The field is added only; no recorded content changes.

WP4e (owner decision D2 revised) records the effective permission mode (free default / safe) on the compiled workflow and the run; pi-workflow had no permission mode. Added only; free mode honors the spec worktreePolicy as pi-workflow did, so no recorded behavior changes.
